summary: Unexpected edge fanout increasing p99 and end-to-end latency across regions after residency pin refresh
description: Issue summary: Customer reports sudden increase in p99 and end-to-end latency for inference requests originating from eu-west and us-east after an automated residency pin refresh window. Impact: Intermittent 200–800ms p50 spike and 1.2–2.6s p99 increase measured by the customer's telemetry; user-facing timeouts observed in a few request flows. Environment: Redwood hosted prod for ClearSight (dedicated capacity). Affected regions: us-east (primary) and eu-west (secondary). Steps to reproduce: 1) Send steady stream of inference requests to pinned model endpoint from eu-west (customer client). 2) Wait for automatic pin refresh window (control-plane refresh observed around HH:15 UTC). 3) Observe sudden increase in request fanout and corresponding p99 in customer traces. Observed behavior: After the pin refresh, traffic briefly fans out to multiple edge nodes and triggers extra TLS handshakes/egress hops. End-to-end times show increased TLS handshake count and additional HTTP/2 connection churn. Expected behavior: Pin refresh should be transparent without creating additional concurrent egress paths for a single request flow; p99 should remain stable. Logs/metrics: Customer provided traces showing 3–5 distinct edge handoffs over ~45s window; clear correlation with residency TTL refresh events. No explicit model failover was triggered. Additional context: Customer is on dedicated pool with autoscale enabled. They rely on consistent low-p99 to meet slot booking SLA for interactive products.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:02 - Aisha Patel (Support): Raised after initial customer report; added to triage queue. Customer attached timing traces and sample request IDs. Asking for rapid triage due to SLAs.

2026-03-10 11:18 - Tom Nguyen (SRE): I can reproduce a small fanout in test harness when forcing a pin refresh. Preliminary guess: control plane push causes a short window where requests are routed to both old and new affinity sets. Collecting edge proxy logs and tcpdump on affected egress nodes.

2026-03-10 15:05 - Customer Engineer (ClearSight): We observed persistent p99 increase for ~60s after the scheduled refresh. We see many TLS rehandshakes and short-lived additional connections from our client IP range.

2026-03-11 09:44 - Nina Rios (Routing Eng): Looking at control-plane propagation timestamps — we see an expand/shrink operation where the residency stamp updates but some edge caches don't invalidate immediately. This may cause simultaneous routing to two edge sets for a brief window.

2026-03-11 14:30 - Tom Nguyen (SRE): Captured edge-proxy logs (edge-proxy@us-east-3) showing duplicate upstream connection attempts for the same request id. Opening GH PR to add more conservative pin-roll logic (see related PR).

2026-03-12 08:20 - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer confirmed a mitigation test: disabling automatic pin refresh eliminated the p99 spikes in a canary environment. They request a recommended short-term workaround and ETA for permanent fix.

2026-03-12 12:10 - Tom Nguyen (SRE): Proposed workaround: increase pin TTL to avoid frequent refresh windows and enable sticky-edge affinity on dedicated pools. We're preparing a controlled rollout of the pin-roll debounce change next week.
2026-03-12 16:00 - Customer Engineer (ClearSight): Acknowledged workaround and asked for written guidance and rollback plan.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10: Initial traces show correlation between control-plane residency stamp refresh and multi-node egress attempts. No model version change detected.
2026-03-10: Edge proxy logs show duplicate upstream connect attempts with shared request ID; connection reuse failed and new TLS handshakes were initiated.
2026-03-11: DNS at edge level appears stable; root cause is not DNS rebind but cache invalidation race in the control plane -> edge subscription path.

2026-03-11: Hypothesis: Pin refresh publishes both old and new routing stamps for a short interval; some edges read the new stamp while others still accept sessions for the old stamp, resulting in request-level fanout.
2026-03-11: Reproduced in internal staging by artificially shortening pin TTL and triggering refresh; p99 increased transiently by ~1.8s on average during the window.
2026-03-11: Related PR created to debounce stamp propagation and avoid overlapping valid stamp windows (https://github.com/redwood/edge-proxy/pull/1423).
2026-03-12: Determined that dedicated pools with autoscale exacerbate the effect because new nodes subscribe during refresh windows and create additional valid upstream targets.
2026-03-12: No evidence of noisy-neighbor GPU saturation; metrics show CPU and net spikes consistent with extra TLS handshakes rather than model inference load.
resolution_notes: Short-term workaround provided to customer: 1) Increase residency pin TTL on endpoint to reduce refresh frequency; 2) Enable sticky-edge affinity option for dedicated pools; 3) Schedule pin refresh during low-traffic windows. Customer confirmed reduced p99 after applying workaround in their canary.
Planned medium-term fix: Deploy debounce logic in control plane that ensures old stamp remains authoritative until all edges acknowledge new stamp, preventing overlap windows. PR#1423 under review.
Rollout plan: canary rollout to 5% of dedicated pools week of 2026-03-22, monitor p99 and handoff counts. Full rollout conditional on no regression after 48h canary.
Follow-ups: 1) Add a runbook entry for customers on how to adjust pin TTL and affinity settings; 2) Add telemetry alerting on edge-fanout events (high TLS handshake rate correlated with pin refresh).
Status: In Progress — SRE and Routing Engs collaborating on PR review and canary schedule. Customer has a mitigation and is notified of timeline.
